messages.text:
I have the DC04 but it doesn't have a UK plug or Harlo OS. Lucky I had a spare 'kettle cable'. I could not install Harlow OS as each time I connect the lillyGo there is an error saying there is interference.

Andrew T.
Note to the team: Handed to our technical specialist, who picks up Andrew's message from here.

I have plugged the lillyGo in and it is listed as COM3 in device manager. There is an error that comes up afylter I connect the devices ce to the Harlow labs site via the popup window    I have tried to find out but I cant find which of the buttons is BOOT.

Andrew T.
Note to the team: Passed to our technical specialist, who replies to Andrew directly in this thread.

I have the Hammer bc04 now but I in conversation with hel at support as I get an error with uploading Harlo OS.

Andrew T.

I get the error after I have chosen Hammer BC04 and selected COM3 from the pop-up window. After a second or so I get the attached

Andrew T.
Note to the team: Handed to our technical specialist with the screenshot, who replies to Andrew in this thread.

I used a usb c port at the back of my PC. First I tried holding BOOT then plugging in, counting to 3 then letting go. I still get the same error when I open Harlow labs and select COM3. I then tried closing the web page, holding BOOT again, plugging in, counting to 3, this time I pressed RST before opening the site selecting BC04 and selecting COM3. On both occasions the screen goes blank for a few seconds then looks like its booting Thor OS then a message flashes on the screen briefly saying 'Power Board Error' in a green box with a orange border. It is now mining again on Thor OS as before.

Andrew T.

Hi Andrew,

That last detail is the answer to the question I had. The module booting into Thor OS means it never entered download mode, so the flasher was talking to a running miner rather than a waiting bootloader. That is exactly what produces the invalid head of packet error, and it is why the sequence matters more than the cable.

The order that works is this. Plug the module in first and leave it plugged in. Press and hold BOOT, and keep holding it. While still holding BOOT, tap RESET once and let RESET go. Keep BOOT held for about three more seconds after that, then release it. The screen should stay dark and should not boot Thor OS. Only then open the Harlo page, choose Hammer BC04 and select COM3. If the display comes up at all, it did not take, so repeat it before touching the site.

The green Power Board Error flashing by as it boots is worth a second pair of eyes, so I have asked JD, who looks after this firmware, to come in on it. The team picks this up today at 10am ET and his answer comes to your email. If you want him faster, he is on our Discord as (contact hidden), and he is very active there.

A colleague also has the UK cord question and will confirm that to you today.

Hal

The lilygo seems to ignore the buttons and go to Thor OS no matter if I plug it in before pressing and holding BOOT or after. Pressing RST seems to do very little as well.

Andrew T.

Hi Andrew,

If both buttons do nothing, then the problem is not the sequence and I am not going to have you repeat it a fourth time. Either the buttons are not the two you think they are, or that module is not dropping into download mode at all, and the green Power Board Error flashing past on boot makes me want a proper look at the board rather than another guess from me.

So I have put this in front of JD, who looks after this firmware and the Harlo OS side. One thing that will speed him up a lot: take a clear photo of the module out of the case, showing the edge with the USB C socket and both small buttons, and send it back in this thread. He can then tell you exactly which one is BOOT, or tell us the module needs replacing.

JD picks this up today from 10am ET and his reply comes to your email. If you would rather not wait, he is on our Discord as (contact hidden), and he answers there quickly. Worth saying plainly, your BC04 mines perfectly well on Thor OS in the meantime, so nothing is at risk.

The U. cord is still with a colleague and they will confirm that to you today as well.

Hal

This is what I think the buttons are.

Andrew T.

Hi Andrew,

That photo answers it. There are two identical little tactile buttons down the right hand edge, one above the USB C socket, which is the one you marked Boot, and a second one directly below the USB C socket. That lower one is the pair to it. The line you drew for Reset points past it at the bare board, so if you have been pressing around there, you have been pressing nothing at all, which explains why Reset seemed to do very little.

Worth one more go with the right pair. Leave it plugged in, hold the upper button, tap the lower one once, keep the upper one held for about three seconds more, then let go. The screen should stay dark. Only then open the Harlo page, pick Hammer BC04 and select COM3.

JD still has this in case that does not take, and he is quickest on Discord as (contact hidden). Otherwise his reply comes to your email from 10am ET today.

Hal
